reason: Conversation 1 correctly identified WTG8 as a condenser dryer, led the homeowner from the front to the hidden pump sump (where grey slime was found and cleaning produced a real 60-minute improvement), then proposed a sensible cup-of-water test to distinguish residual blockage from a weak or failed pump before escalating to an engineer, remaining honest about the uncertainty. Conversation 2 prematurely and repeatedly labelled the fault a 'float switch' without any supporting checks, wrongly called the machine a heat-pump dryer, pushed a parts-lookup panel, and never mentioned the pump sump at all, so the homeowner got no useful self-help before being sent to an engineer. Conversation 1's main lapses are not telling the customer to unplug before cleaning the sump and an early tilt suggestion that became moot once the stacked setup was revealed, but these are minor against conversation 2's unsupported diagnosis and missed sensible first step.
